Spotter · Privacy policy · Terms of use · What’s new

Spotter

By Quarterdeck Collective

Save a workout video. Make it your next session.

Spotter turns fitness videos into workout cards you can follow and log. Save a link from TikTok, Instagram or YouTube, review the exercises, sets and reps, and train one movement at a time.

Open Spotter

Your training, in one place

  • Save and organize workouts with favorites and collections.
  • Track sets, reps and weights in Workout Mode.
  • Plan your week and review your workout history and progress.
  • Ask Pumpy to help build or adapt a workout, then review and confirm its suggested changes.

Your account and your data

Sign in with email or an available sign-in provider. Your account connects your library, workout logs and settings across Spotter’s web and iPhone apps. Read our privacy policy to learn what information Spotter uses and how to export or delete your account, and our terms of use before using the app.

Spotter provides fitness guidance. Review extracted workouts before following them.

Contact

For questions about Spotter or your account, email business@quarterdeckcollective.com.

item.content:encoded:
Spotter · Privacy policy · Terms of use · What’s new

Spotter Privacy Policy

Last updated 8 September 2026

Spotter is a small, independent app. This page says plainly what it stores and what it does not do. If anything here is unclear, email business@quarterdeckcollective.com.

What Spotter stores

  • Your email address and password. Handled by Supabase Auth; the password is stored only as a salted hash and is never visible to us.
  • If you continue with Google or Apple, Spotter receives only your name and your email address from them — nothing else, and no password ever reaches us; Apple lets you hide your real address behind a private relay, and that relay address works here.
  • The videos you save — the link, the creator name, the caption or description that was public on the post, and the workout extracted from it.
  • What you log — the sets, reps and weights you record in Workout Mode, plus any notes and planned days you add.
  • A personal save key so an iOS Shortcut can add videos for you. You can replace it any time from Settings.
  • Your conversations with Pumpy, the coach, so you can pick a chat up where you left it, and the changes you confirmed from them. They are private to your account.
  • If you subscribe to Spotter Plus, an identifier for you at Stripe and the state of your subscription — the plan, whether it is running, and the date it renews or ends. Never your card. See Payments below.

What Spotter does not do

  • No ads, no trackers, no analytics scripts, no cookies beyond the sign-in session your browser needs.
  • Your library, logs and plan are private to your account and are not sold. Relevant details are processed by the service providers described below when you use AI features.
  • Spotter does not access device health, biometric or location sensors. Workout logs are fitness information, and anything you type into notes or Pumpy may include sensitive information.

Other services involved

Saving a post can send its caption, description, carousel images, or text you supply to OpenAI to extract exercises. Google Gemini is used only for supported audio/video reads. Text, coaching and image requests do not automatically fall back to Google. Private uploads can also be processed by Google. Groq is no longer part of the active reading workflow.

Asking Pumpy, tapping How to do this, or Swap or modify also sends an AI model what you typed plus what it needs to answer: the titles, exercises, equipment and collection names of the workouts you have saved, your planned days, and a summary of your recent sessions (how many, which muscles, how much volume). Pumpy sends a short index of that — titles, categories, equipment, collection names, your planned days — at the start of every message so it needs fewer round trips, and sends a workout's exercises only when it needs them to answer. Account email is not deliberately included in these requests. Text you put in a message, exercise detail or selected workout may be included, so avoid adding sensitive information unnecessarily. Pumpy cannot change anything in your library until you confirm it in the app.

Data is stored with Supabase in the United States. Fonts are loaded from Google Fonts.

Video playback happens in an embedded player from Instagram, TikTok or YouTube. Those players are the platforms' own and follow the platforms' privacy policies.

When you ask how an exercise is done, Spotter shows a short demonstration clip. These come from a short list of fitness creators' public YouTube channels, collected in advance and stored by exercise, so most of the time nothing is looked up at all — the answer is already in Spotter's own list, and more than one creator may be offered for the same movement. For a movement that list does not cover, the server falls back to searching YouTube, preferring those same channels. Either way only the name of the exercise is sent — never your email, your account or anything else about you — and any search result is cached and shared by everyone, so the same movement is looked up once for all of Spotter rather than once per person. The thumbnail is loaded from Google's image host, and the clip, if you tap it, plays in a privacy-enhanced (no-cookie) YouTube player that is only added to the page once you tap and is removed again when you close the sheet. The link beside it opens YouTube's own search results.

Payments

Spotter Plus is paid for through Stripe, and the payment happens on Stripe's own checkout page, not on Spotter's. Your card number, the security code on the back of it and whatever address your bank wants go to Stripe and stop there. Spotter never sees any of it, has no way to ask for it, and could not charge your card by itself if it wanted to.

What Spotter keeps, on a row attached to your account, is only what it needs to know whether you are on the paid plan today:

  • the customer and subscription identifiers Stripe gave you, so the two systems can talk about the same person;
  • which plan it is, whether it is on trial, running, cancelled or unpaid, whether it is set to stop at the end of the period, and the date that period ends;
  • the date a payment last failed, if one has, so the app can say so and offer the fix;
  • a log of the notifications Stripe sends — the identifier and type of each one, and when it was handled. That log is how Spotter avoids acting on the same message twice. It holds no payment details.

Stripe is its own company and handles your payment data under its own privacy policy. Spotter sends it your account identifier so a payment can be matched back to you, and your email address if you give Stripe one at checkout.

If you cancel, the row stays until the period you paid for runs out and then says you are on the free plan. Deleting your account cancels the subscription first, then deletes your customer record at Stripe along with everything else. Stripe keeps its own record of the payments themselves for as long as tax and accounting law says it must — that part is not Spotter's to delete.

Connections

Spotter can connect to Strava, if you choose to, so that a workout you have just finished can be sent there as an activity. You connect it yourself in Settings → Connections, and nothing happens until you do.

The connection is one-way. Spotter writes to Strava and never reads from it: it does not see your activities, your friends, your routes, your segments or your profile, and no Strava data is ever given to any of the AI services above. What gets sent, and only when you tap Send to Strava on a session, is the workout's name, when you started it and how long it took, one line per exercise with the sets you logged, your total volume, any personal bests from that session, and a link back to Spotter.

When you connect, Strava gives Spotter's server two access keys. They are held on a row attached to your account on the server only — the app in your browser never receives them and cannot read them — together with your Strava athlete number and the identifier of each activity Spotter created, so the same session is never posted twice. Disconnecting deletes both keys and tells Strava to forget Spotter, and so does deleting your account. You can also revoke Spotter yourself at any time from your Strava settings.

Files and video reading

Uploads enter private temporary storage. Spotter's server sends supported audio or video to Google Gemini for transcription or workout extraction. Spotter attempts to delete its temporary file and Google's uploaded file after processing, including failed attempts. A cleanup sweep targets files left in Spotter storage after two hours; outages can delay cleanup. Extracted text and workout details remain on your saved card.

For public links with little written workout information, Spotter may also read available audio or video, automatically or when you request it. Source material fetched from a public post may contribute to the shared cache below. Your private uploads and supplied captions or HTML are excluded from new shared cache entries.

Deleting a temporary uploaded file does not erase a provider's separate processing or abuse monitoring records. Provider handling depends on the account and service configuration; see OpenAI's data controls and Google's API terms. In particular, Google's paid and unpaid services have different data-use terms.

Shared extraction cache

When a video is read for the first time, the resulting workout is cached under the video's public ID so the next person who saves the same video gets it instantly and no AI call is needed. That cache holds only information taken from the public post — never anything about who saved it. It is not linked to any account, so deleting an account does not remove it.

Taking your data with you

Settings → Data & privacy → Export my data writes everything you put into Spotter — your workout cards, every session you have logged, your plan, your collections, your chats with Pumpy and your settings — into a single JSON file on your device. It is a plain, structured, machine-readable format, so you can read it yourself or move it somewhere else. Your personal save key is deliberately left out of the file, because it works without a password and files get forwarded.

Deleting your account

Removing a workout deletes it immediately. To delete your whole account, open Spotter and go to Settings → Data & privacy → Delete account. You will be asked to type DELETE to confirm, and then the following are removed from the active app:

  • your workout cards, and any video files you uploaded;
  • every session you have logged, and your plan;
  • your collections and the corrections you made to cards;
  • your chats with Pumpy;
  • your profile, your settings and your personal save key;
  • your subscription, if you have one — it is cancelled at Stripe first, and your customer record there is deleted with it;
  • your Strava connection, if you made one — Strava is told to forget Spotter and both access keys are deleted;
  • the sign-in account itself.

Export your data first if you want to keep it. Account deletion cannot be undone in the app. Backup copies and provider security records may remain under their separate retention policies. Spotter keeps its own record of what the AI cost to run, and the deletion strips your account id out of those rows rather than keeping them attached to you. New AI reservation records are retained for up to 90 days; request admission records for up to 40 days, with scheduled cleanup.

If you cannot sign in, email business@quarterdeckcollective.com from your account's address and it will be erased for you.

item.title: Spotter Terms of Use
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Spotter · Privacy policy · Terms of use · What’s new

Spotter Terms of Use

Last updated 4 September 2026

Spotter is a small, independent app made by one person. These terms are the agreement between you and Spotter. They are written plainly on purpose. If anything here is unclear, open an issue at github.com/SimeonRinkenberger/spotter/issues and ask.

What Spotter is

You save a link to a fitness video. Spotter reads what is publicly attached to that video — the caption, the description, and where those say nothing, the audio or the words on screen — and turns it into a workout card you can follow and log. It also gives you a weekly plan, a progress view, and a coach called Pumpy who can build workouts out of what you have saved.

Spotter does not host the videos. It links to them and shows the platforms' own players.

Your account

You need an account, and you must be at least 13 years old to have one — the same age Spotter's privacy policy is written around. One person, one account. Keep your password to yourself, and keep your personal save key private: it works without a password, which is the point of it and also the risk.

You can delete your account at any time from Settings → Data & privacy → Delete account. That erases your cards, sessions, plan, collections and chats, permanently, and cancels any subscription first.

Spotter Plus

AI reading and coaching have per-account daily and monthly usage limits. During beta, shared service allowances can also pause new AI work, including on paid plans. Saved workouts remain available. A subscription does not include unlimited AI requests.

Spotter Plus is an optional paid subscription that raises the limits on the free plan. It renews by itself until you cancel it. Payment is taken by Stripe, which is the merchant of record for the charge; Spotter never sees your card number.

  • Monthly or yearly. The price you see on the plan screen at the moment you subscribe is the price you pay, in US dollars, and it is charged again at the start of each period until you cancel.
  • The free trial is on the yearly plan. It runs for seven days. A payment method is collected when you start it, and the card is charged when the trial ends unless you cancel before then. Cancelling during the trial costs nothing.
  • The founding price applies to the first year only. If you take it, the following year renews at the standard yearly price, which is shown on the plan screen at the time you subscribe.
  • Cancel any time, from Settings → Plan → Manage subscription. Cancelling stops the next renewal; Plus keeps working until the end of the period you have already paid for, and then the account returns to the free plan. Nothing you saved is deleted — your cards stay in your library and stay readable, whatever plan you are on.
  • Refunds. Payments already taken are not refunded in part when you cancel partway through a period, except where the law where you live requires it. If something has gone genuinely wrong, ask — the issues page above is the way to.
  • Prices can change. If the price of a plan you are on changes, you will be told at least 30 days in advance, and the new price applies from your next renewal, not before. You can cancel in the meantime.
  • Spotter may change what the free plan and the paid plan include. If a change removes something you are paying for, it takes effect at your next renewal.

How you may use Spotter

Save links you found yourself, for your own training. Do not scrape or automate the service, do not resell access to it, do not try to get around the limits on your plan, and do not use it to attack anyone or anything. Spotter's servers are small and shared, and the daily limits exist so one account cannot take the day away from everybody else.

Videos and the cards made from them

The videos belong to the creators who made them. Spotter's cards are derived from what those creators published publicly, and a card is a summary of exercises, not a copy of the video. You keep whatever you write yourself — your notes, your logs, your corrections.

If you are a creator and you want a card made from your video taken down, open an issue at the issues page saying which video it is, and it will be removed. That page is the contact point for copyright complaints until there is a formal one.

This is not medical advice

Spotter is training guidance, not medical advice, and neither Spotter nor Pumpy is a doctor, a physiotherapist or a coach who can see you. Exercises are read out of videos made by other people and may be wrong, unsuitable for you, or unsafe for how you train. If something hurts, stop, and see a professional. Talk to a doctor before starting a new programme, especially if you are injured, pregnant, or managing a condition. You lift at your own risk.

Availability

Spotter is offered as it is, with no promise that it will be available, correct, or free of faults. It runs on services other people operate and reads platforms other people control, so features can break without warning — a platform blocking access is the most likely reason a save will fail. Where the law allows it, Spotter is not liable for losses arising from using it, and any liability that cannot be excluded is limited to what you have paid in the previous twelve months.

Ending this

You can stop using Spotter and delete your account whenever you like. Spotter may suspend or close an account that is being used to attack the service, to break these terms, or in a way that is plainly not personal use. If that happens to a paying account for a reason that is not your fault, the unused part of the period is refunded.

Law

These terms are governed by the laws of the State of Illinois, United States, without regard to conflict-of-law rules, and the courts of Illinois are where any dispute is heard.

Changes and contact

If these terms change materially, the date at the top changes and the app says so. Continuing to use Spotter after that means the new terms apply. For anything at all — a question, a complaint, a takedown — use the issues page.

item.title: Spotter — What’s New
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Spotter · Privacy policy · Terms of use · What’s new

Spotter — What’s New

Everything that has changed in Spotter, newest first.

Pumpy stays with you

Version 0.12 · 6 September 2026

  • Pumpy keeps giving a quiet blink while his greeting is on screen. It pauses when you leave or cover the page, and respects Reduce Motion and Little animations.
  • “Ask Pumpy about this workout” now shows the workout attached beside your message box. It stays selected even if an older chat finishes loading afterward.

A warmer welcome, a calmer coach

Version 0.11 · 6 September 2026

  • New here? Three short, skippable steps show how to save, find your workouts and open Pumpy. Replay them from the Quick guide whenever you like.
  • Pumpy has more expression: thoughtful while planning, pleased after a workout, and relaxed against the rack when you meet him.
  • A small blink and smoother wing movement play once, then settle. Reduce Motion and the Little animations setting keep everything still.
  • Help rows expand smoothly, tips dismiss without a jump, and the introduction keeps its buttons in place between steps.

Meet your coach

Version 0.10 · 6 September 2026

  • Pumpy has a new look, with illustrated poses for getting started, planning and finishing a session.
  • A little help where you need it: short, dismissible tips for saving, exercise options, logging, planning and Pumpy’s workout picker.
  • A quiet wing movement at a finish, then stillness. Reduce Motion is respected, and Settings lets you turn Pumpy’s tips and animations off.
  • Settings → Pumpy → Quick guide brings the help back whenever you want it.
  • Saving a preference now preserves other saved settings.

Handcrafted, not generated

Version 0.9 · 2 September 2026

  • Every emoji standing in for an icon is gone. Spotter now has a drawn icon set that looks the same on an iPhone as it does on a Pixel, and that a screen reader can name.
  • Deleting a session, a collection or an exercise can be undone. Nothing is actually removed until the message offering the undo has gone.
  • When something goes wrong, Spotter says what failed and what to do about it instead of “could not do that”.
  • Fixed: a session finished in the evening could tick the wrong day on your plan if you live far enough from London. The plan now uses your own calendar day.
  • Pull to refresh tells you what it found — how many workouts came in, or that you were already up to date.
  • The Progress figures count up when you open the tab, and the numbers stop jittering as they change.
  • Every button now shows a focus ring when you tab to it with a keyboard.
  • Pumpy’s three dots move while it is thinking, instead of sitting there.
  • A quieter set of small labels throughout, and this page, a version number and a way to report something wrong at the bottom of Settings.

Swipe between tabs, and a workout worth opening in a gym

2 September 2026

  • The four tabs are one surface you can swipe between, with the titles and the tab bar moving with your finger rather than jumping when a screen swaps.
  • Workout Mode gained a rest timer you can pause, extend or skip; a “watch the clip” button for when the name of a movement is not enough; and a session summary at the end with your time, sets, volume and anything you beat.
  • The Library answers “what am I doing today” at the top of the screen, and the creator of a video is now something you can filter by.

Share straight to Spotter, and let it watch the video

2 September 2026

  • On Android, install Spotter and it appears in the share sheet: send any video to it without opening the app. On iPhone the Shortcut is still the route.
  • Some creators say the workout out loud, or write it on the screen, and put none of it in the caption. Spotter can now listen to the video, and read what is written in it.
  • Continue with Google and Continue with Apple, without being thrown out of the app to a browser and back.
  • Every screen arrives and leaves on purpose, the light colours were brought up to the AA contrast standard, and reduced-motion settings are honoured throughout.

Pumpy, the coach

1 September 2026

  • A coach that can see what you have saved, what you have planned and what you have logged. It can build a workout, add to one or plan your week — and shows you what it wants to do before anything is saved.
  • An anatomical body map: what a workout hits, and what you have hit this week.
  • Ask for a swap when the equipment is missing, the station is busy, or something hurts, and get honest trade-offs rather than a list.
  • Collections, renaming, and the ability to correct an exercise Spotter got wrong.
  • Upload a video you already saved and Spotter will listen to it.
  • History moved into Progress, which freed a tab.

The first version

31 August 2026

  • Paste a link to a TikTok, Instagram reel or YouTube video and Spotter reads the exercises, sets and reps out of it.
  • Workout Mode: one movement at a time, logging what you lift, with what you did last time already filled in.
  • A week view for planning, and a Progress tab for volume, records and streaks.

Something wrong, or something missing? Tell me here.
